result.document_summary: Berkeley Rent Board web page describing state and local limits on tenant screening fees and application fees, including BMC chapter 13.78 requirements.
result.notes: Two records extracted: the state screening-fee cap and rules (Cal. Civ. Code 1950.6, as summarized by the City page) and the Berkeley local ordinance (BMC ch. 13.78). The page gives no effective dates for either. Coverage is not limited by the page beyond residential rental property. The 2026 cap figure of $68.96 comes from the page.

rules.title: California tenant screening fee cap and requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a capped screening fee for obtaining information like a credit report, and must provide a receipt, itemized costs, a copy of the report, and a refund of any unused portion. No fee may be charged if no unit is available, and fees must be returned to applicants not selected unless the landlord reviews applications in order received and charges no one not considered.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to landlords charging screening fees to prospective tenants of residential rental units; the page states no further coverage tests.
rules.interaction: The Berkeley page notes the state limit applies in Berkeley and that BMC 13.78.010 requires disclosure of the state fee cap.

rules.title: Berkeley screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners charging a fee for a credit report or application processing must provide a clear tenant screening fee rights statement and the state maximum fee cap before receiving the fee. Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy or for adding, replacing, or removing a roommate.
rules.key_value: Disclosure of Cal. Civ. Code 1950.6(b) fee cap; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley regardless of contrary lease language.
rules.interaction: Incorporates the state screening fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code 1950.6(b); lease provisions violating the chapter are unenforceable.
